reference.notes:
I implemented `applyPatch` and every test passes: public 30/30 and private 79/79, run with `npm run build && node sandbox/run.mjs public|private`.

The code is in three files under `src/`:
- **`src/main.go`**: keeps the contract comment. It reads `[files, diff]` from stdin and writes the result as JSON on stdout. If the diff is malformed, it writes only the error message on stderr and exits 1.
- **`src/parse.go`**: reads the diff into one section per file. A hunk is read by its header's line counts, so hunk lines that start with `---`, `+++` or `@@` stay part of the hunk. A hunk with fewer lines than its header counts is an error, and so is a hunk before any file header; the "No newline at end of file" marker doesn't count as a line.
- **`src/apply.go`**: applies each hunk where it matches nearest its stated line, never before the end of the hunk before it, and only on an exact match. It keeps each file's line endings and handles a missing final newline as the spec describes. Changes are made to a copy of the files, and any rejection returns the original files untouched.

Choices I made where the spec is silent (no test covers them):
- **No newline marker:** a hunk line without the marker only matches a file line that ends with a newline. This is what git does.
- **Deleting a non-empty file with no hunks:** rejected as `"no match"` and reported as hunk 1, since there is no real hunk to number.
- **Renaming onto a path that already has a file:** rejected as `"exists"` rather than overwriting that file.

I also ran the command directly on a few header-less cases from the spec: creating an empty file, deleting an empty file, and a rename with no hunks all apply.

To build outside `npm run build`, I had to set `GOCACHE` to the temp folder, because the sandbox blocks the default Go cache. The build script already does this, so nothing in the project changed.

Tests left failing: none
